**Stage 10 restores the GO bar on everything** before the public release: every changed line's
mutants killed or ruled, across tiers.

### Mutation testing: are the tests any good?

Coverage says a line ran under a test; it cannot say the test would notice the line being
wrong. **Mutation testing** changes the code one small way at a time (a `<` for a `<=`, a
constant, a dropped argument), runs the tests that reach it, and counts the **mutants** the tests
**kill** (some test fails) against those that **survive** (every test still passes). A survivor
is either a missing assertion (a behaviour nobody pins) or an **equivalent mutant**, a change no
behaviour can observe (a debug message's words).

The tool is mutmut 3.8.0 (BSD-3; dev-only: not in the runtime requirements, not in the gate,
never run per push; its pins are `requirements-mutation.txt`), run inside the same
loopback-only namespace as the suite, with CI's interpreter.

**One mutant at a time, always (`--max-children 1`).** The suite's test store is chosen once
per process image, when `tests/conftest.py` is imported, and a session's end removes it. mutmut
forks its children from one process that has already imported the conftest, so parallel
children share that one store, and the first to finish deletes it from under the rest: their
tests fail, and mutmut counts every such failure as a kill. Measured 2026-10-14: in parallel,
mutants that only change a `log.debug` call were "killed" and two runs disagreed; serially, two
runs agreed mutant for mutant; and six SEPARATE processes running the same 192 tests at once
all passed, so the tests share no fixed path, port or file (the gate's shards and xdist's
workers are separate processes, each with its own store). It is mutmut's fork model meeting
the harness's per-process store, not tests leaking into each other. A kill nobody can explain
is the sign. The first pass's published figure was made in parallel and was wrong (C766); the
table below is its serial re-run.

**A test's child process** (a test that runs one of Mercury's scripts) cannot record mutmut's
statistics: recording needs mutmut's configuration, which only the run's own folder holds, and
a child started elsewhere raised `FileNotFoundError` and failed the run (measured 2026-10-14,
walking `config_check`). Under the statistics run the harness's spawn guard starts every child
with `MUTMUT_DEPENDENCY_DEPTH=0`, so it records nothing (its hits would die with it anyway);
under a mutant's run the child runs the mutant, so a test that spawns can still kill it.

**The first pass (2026-10-14)**, on two automation modules, against their own test files
(`tests/test_dhcp_subnets.py`, `tests/test_hostvars_secrets.py`), serially:

| Function | Mutants | Killed before | Killed after | Known equivalent | Left |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dhcp_subnets.pool_span` (the pool helper) | 30 | 25 | 27 | 3 | 0 |
| `dhcp_subnets._pools_of` | 15 | 11 | 12 | 3 | 0 |
| `hostvars._looks_hashed` (hash detection) | 24 | 18 | 20 | 4 | 0 |
| `hostvars.assert_printable` (the ASCII rule) | 15 | 9 | 14 | 0 | 1 (C767, since fixed) |
| `hostvars.assert_no_secret_values` | 48 | 29 | 38 | 10 | 0 |
| **All** | **132** | **92 (69.7%)** | **111 (84.1%)** | **20** | **1** |

Over the 112 mutants a test could kill (all, less the 20 equivalents), the tests kill 111
(99.1%). Of the 20 real survivors, 19 are now killed, each by a test naming it in its docstring.
First among them: the secret check skips another device's secret, or one too short to check,
with `continue`, and `break` in its place (ending the scan, so a leak listed after the skipped
secret would pass: a guard failing open) survived every test. The CODE was always right (both
skips have been `continue` since the loop was written, 081124c6); no test would have caught it
being broken. The rest: the check's length floor, a `secrets:` mapping on line 1, the words of
both refusals, `$5$` and `$8$` hashes, a prefix with host bits, a bad pool ending a subnet's
read, the printable refusal's words. The one left was `assert_printable`'s column, counted
across the whole file rather than within the line (C767): the message only, never what is
refused. Fixed the same day (line by line, "line N, column M"); the rewritten function's 25
mutants are all killed.

**The rule (the operator, 2026-10-25; the testing model, approved the same day; "The deploy
bar" above):** mutation runs weekly, scheduled, outside 08:30 to 09:10 UTC, as a measurement;
survivors are registered, not worked, unless the operator directs a campaign; no other run is
dispatched but a change to the irreversible tier, whose targeted run comes before its deploy.
(The interim rule of the same night, "no on-demand dispatches", ran from runs #58 to #61 to
this approval: no continuation, targeted run or re-run was dispatched in it.)

**The weekly run** (`.github/workflows/mutation-nightly.yml`, Sunday 14:00 UTC; never on a push
or a pull request). A schedule can start hours late (C772 measured 5 h 26 min), so its first
job, `window`, reads the clock and refuses a start inside 08:30 to 09:10 UTC: nothing is
mutated, the run says why, and the next week's runs as usual. The dispatch trigger stays for an
irreversible tier's targeted run and a campaign the operator directs; nothing else uses it.
[tests/test_nmas_mutation.py, `TestTheWorkflow`: one weekly cron outside the window, the guard
before the mutation job, the guard's own shell refusing exactly 08:30 to 09:09]

The 2026-10-15 parking (C835, "Phase 7 first") is replaced by this rule. The harness, the
canary, the record and the debt list are as they were, so the weekly run resumes where the
nights stopped. Coverage says a test RAN a line; mutation testing says
whether a test would NOTICE the line being wrong, so a test that calls a function and checks
nothing scores 100% coverage and 0% here. Each run (a "night" below):

- **Scope, changed only:** the counted automation functions (the coverage tool's scope and
  counting rules, `tests/coverage_scope.py`, `scripts/pydefs.py`) whose lines changed since the
  commit the last night covered (on a night with no record, since the commit that added the
  nightly workflow, so the first night is not an empty one), read with `git diff -U0`,
  and the functions the record keeps (below), at most the night's cap of them (below). Each
  function's mutants run against the tests MEASURED to execute it (below); where nothing has
  measured it yet, against the test files whose code imports its module (parsed, never
  searched: a text search matched an import written inside a test's string data). mutmut writes every mutant of a FILE, so its progress
  counter counts the whole file (`x/2168` for `config_check.py`); only the planned functions'
  run, and the report checks it: a mutant of anything else having run is "SCOPE BROKEN" and
  fails the night. `nmas-mutation plan --also path::qualname` names a function to mutate whole,
  changed or not; the Actions tab's Run workflow takes the same as its `functions` input
  (space-separated), passed to the script through the environment.
- **The canary first.** `tests/mutation_canary.py` holds two functions every night mutates
  beside the planned ones: `in_process`, reached only in a test's process, and `in_child`,
  reached only through a child process the test starts, as `config_check`'s tests reach the
  check through `scripts/nmas-config-check`. Every one of their mutants must be killed
  (`tests/test_mutation_canary.py` pins them so). The run mutates them in their own two mutmut
  runs before the night's mutants and stops if any survives: the night fails as "MEASUREMENT
  BROKEN", never as survivors, and no result stands. Shown able to fail twice (2026-10-14):
  children stripped of `MUTANT_UNDER_TEST` (the in-child mutants survived), and the tests that
  start a child left out of the in-child function's tests (they read "no tests").
- **The night's tests, by measured reach** (C796, C834; the operator, 2026-10-15: "the coverage
  nightly's per-test contexts say which tests execute each function, and a mutant runs only
  those"). The workflow downloads the newest successful coverage nightly's `coverage-drilldown`
  (its `coverage.json`, each function's tests by per-test context, and `tiers/`, each test's
  tier record) from that run, with the job's token reading Actions (`actions: read`, the one
  permission it adds; `READS_ACTIONS` in tests/test_ci_workflow.py). For a planned function
  whose text at the drill-down's commit is its text tonight, the night runs the tests the
  contexts saw execute it (by test function, so a moved parameter id still selects; an id head
  no longer collects is dropped and named), its importing files' child-starting tests (their
  children are measured below), and those importing files changed since the drill-down whole
  (their tests are newer than the measurement, as a test written to kill a survivor is). The
  summary says which functions were measured and why each other one was not. Per mutant,
  mutmut's own statistics run then picks, among those, the tests that called the function in
  the test's process. **What a caller's change since the drill-down makes newly reach a
  function whose own text is unchanged is not seen until the next coverage night** (only the
  function's own text hash is compared).
- **A stale map** (the operator, 2026-10-15: "a night selects tests from the coverage
  nightly's artifact, which can be older than the code it mutates"). Every summary names the
  map under its heading: the coverage nightly's run, its commit and date, and why it was not
  usable when it was not, or "none found" (`map_line`; the workflow reads the run's id, head
  commit and `created_at`). A planned function is **stale** when its text hash differs from the
  map's, or the map lacks it (or there is no usable map): the hash is `function_hash`, sha256
  of the function's own lines (nested functions within), of the file at the map's commit (`git
  show <commit>:<path>`) against the same at tonight's head (`reach_fresh`, which records both
  in the plan's `map_hashes`). A stale function is never selected by the map, and never by the
  test files importing its module: a test reaching it only through a caller imports nothing of
  it (C842: `history_ask.alternation`'s killing test). The two ways measured on the laptop
  (2026-10-15, fcd1e4f6, 11,053 tests, 4 workers), against a capped night's 120-minute budget
  that already holds about 60 minutes of setup and 15 of mutants on the runner:
  - **(a) refresh the map in the same workflow, CHOSEN:** the whole suite once, confined, the C
    tracer's per-test contexts over the stale functions' modules alone: **521 s** over 7
    modules, and 825 s over 1 in the planted walk while other suites loaded the laptop; at 2.2
    times about 19 to 30 minutes on the runner. On the runner itself the coverage nightly's own
    four shards' test steps (the same suite per test, every module, with branches) summed
    1,988 s (run #2), 1,646 s (run #3) and 2,070 s (run #4): **about 27 to 35 minutes**, which
    with a capped night's 60 minutes of setup and 15 of mutants is 102 to 110, inside 120 even
    were it counted there. It runs in the plan step, before mutmut and outside the budget's
    `timeout`; the job's bound grows by its own (`REFRESH_TIMEOUT_S`, 5,200 s, about 2.5 times
    run #4's; `timeout-minutes` 230), the budget unchanged.
  - **(b) the whole suite as mutmut's own selection:** cannot run as the night stands (the
    copy lacks `.github/`, which a test reads at collection: mutmut's statistics run failed in
    68 s). With `.github/` copied in a scratch clone: the whole suite in mutmut's copy 360 s
    (53 tests fail there with no mutant active, C779's kind, against 2 for a capped night);
    mutmut's statistics run over it, serial, 1,056 s; its clean run then failed after 253 s and
    2,281 tests, on a test failing only in that order, so no mutant was reached. A night's
    setup repeats these (two statistics runs, three clean runs, the copy run): about 6,100 s
    on the laptop by these figures, about 3.7 hours on the runner, three times the budget.
  - **(c) defer** the stale function until a coverage nightly holds its text: the fallback,
    used when the refresh cannot measure (its bound fired, it crashed, it left no data; or
    `plan --stale-map defer`). The function waits in the record as the cap's deferred ones do
    (its results kept; one not started `whole`), is named in the summary with why ("Stale map,
    not mutated tonight"), and is planned the first night a map holds its text.

  The refresh's tests for each stale function are those its contexts saw execute a line of the
  function's body, in any phase (`refreshed_reach`), with its importing files' tests the
  refresh saw start a child of ours, as for a map-measured function (their children are
  measured each night, below); only ids of this checkout's test files (the refresh's tier
  records also hold the suite's own nested pytest runs' ids). A test that fails in the refresh
  is run once more alone, its contexts appended: one that passes then is measured whole (the
  laptop's refresh had one, `test_v2_brand`'s rendered-page check, failing among the rest and
  passing alone); one that fails again fails on the unmutated code, so it can kill no mutant
  (it would fail mutmut's clean run, and be deselected there, C779), and is named. Only when
  that second run cannot itself finish is the reach partial: its functions are "refreshed in
  part" (the map's own tests for them added), a stale selection.
- **A survivor under a stale selection** (its function's tests not chosen by a measurement of
  its text tonight: anything but `measured` or `refreshed`; a plan from before this rule, by
  import, included) carries `stale_map` in the report, in the summary's survivor line ("STALE
  MAP") and in the record (the function's `stale_map`, an additive field). It is never known
  debt or the baseline sweep's, even when its lines are on the debt list; it is an open VERDICT
  survivor and **fails the night** like any other (the rule stands: only an open VERDICT
  survivor turns it red); and `nmas-mutation debt add` refuses a report holding one, naming
  each, until a night under fresh selection finds it too (`add_to_debt`).
- **The planted case** (the operator's test, 2026-10-15): a function changed after the coverage
  run and a test that only now reaches it, through a caller, importing nothing of it.
  `TestAStaleMap` holds it in a real repository with a real refresh (the caller's test found,
  the planted mutant killed by that selection and surviving the import one); walked on the
  laptop through the night's three steps (2026-10-15, at fcd1e4f6): commit A added
  `toy_walk.span`, mapped by the coverage tool's own report; commit B changed it and added a
  test reaching it only through `toy_walk_caller.width`. The plan judged it stale by its hash,
  the refresh (762 s; 930 s on a second walk, the laptop loaded) selected
  `test_toy_walk.py::test_never_negative` and
  `test_toy_walk_caller.py::test_width`, and mutmut's 3 mutants were all killed, `hi - lo + 1`
  → `hi + lo + 1` among them. The same night under af2a439a's selection (by import:
  `tests/test_toy_walk.py`) left that one and `+ 1` → `+ 2` surviving.
- **A test's child.** A child process records nothing in mutmut's statistics (above), and the
  coverage nightly's contexts do not see it either (measured 2026-10-15 with CI's coverage
  command, coverage 7.16.1 and pytest-cov 7.1.0, which no longer measures children: `in_child`'s
  body line had no context at all). Proven on `config_check._check_device` (2026-10-14) that
  children do run planned code: a mutant's own code, instrumented to record the process running
  it, ran in 12 separate `nmas-config-check` children per test run. So each night, after the
  first run records each test's tier and its count of children of ours (`children`, counted by
  the spawn guard; `tests/conftest.py`), every test that started one is run once more, in the
  checkout, with coverage in its children: the spawn guard gives every child a test starts
  `COVERAGE_PROCESS_START` (when `NMAS_CHILD_COVERAGE` names the night's configuration) and the
  test's id as its coverage context, and every Python child runs the guard's sitecustomize, so a
  measured child always writes its test's context. A test joins only the functions its children
  ran (`child_reach`); one that failed there, was not reached, or has fewer measured children
  than it started joins every function, as before, and is named in the summary. The canary's
  `in_child` gets `test_in_child` only through this measurement, so a measurement that
  misattributes kills the canary's verdict, not the night's.
- **A labelled dispatch** (Lab 9, 2026-10-23, the operator: groups of functions measured in
  parallel): the `label` input (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens; anything else refused by
  the plan step) gives the run its own concurrency group, `mutation-nightly-<label>`, beside
  the night and other labels, and saves its record under `mutation-group-<label>-<run>`,
  outside the `mutation-state-` prefix a night restores: its verdict stands in its run alone.
  A labelled run restores its own group's newest record first, then the nights', so a function
  its budget cut short continues on the next run of the same label (2026-10-23, run #34). A
  NAMED function the record holds unfinished at its very text runs only its unchecked and open
  mutants, its results kept (runs #34 and #36 had re-run `_phases` whole, 448 mutants, and
  stopped at the same mutant twice); one the record does not hold is still mutated whole.
  Dispatched with `functions` and a `cap` equal to their count, it runs only those.
  [tests/test_nmas_mutation.py, `TestTheWorkflow`]
- **The cap** (C834): at most `NIGHT_CAP` functions a night (`plan --cap`), the oldest
  unfinished first: a function a person named tonight, then by when each entered the record
  (`since`, the head commit of the night it entered; a record from before the field is older
  than any), then the functions changed tonight. The rest wait in the record as they were
  (results kept; one not started as `whole`) and are named in the summary. The copy run, the
  statistics run and the clean runs then see only the capped plan's tests. **Walked on the
  laptop, 2026-10-15** (the night's steps at ff55539b, the coverage nightly of f48fdc617):
  - `onboard.create_netbox_record` alone: by import, 29 test files and every child-starting
    test, the run took 814 s, survivors 0.8 s and killed 0.2 s each (mutmut's
    `durations_by_key`); by measured reach, 14 test functions, the run took 146 s, survivors
    0.5 s; the same 104 killed and 129 survived, mutant for mutant. Of its 4 child-starting
    tests, 3 were measured (`test_in_child` reaching only the canary's `in_child`) and 1, whose
    child the test kills, was not, so it joined every function.
  - the record night #12 left (92 functions waiting), capped at 20: 16 measured, 4 by import
    (changed since the drill-down, or new), 51 test files whole and 412 test functions where
    import alone would run 134 files; the copy run 183 s for 1,833 tests; the children of 21
    tests measured in 9 s (18 measured, 3 not), 59 associations added where every test joining
    every function would add 462; the canary all killed; 72 functions left waiting, named. On
    the laptop everything before the first mutant took about 27 minutes (the statistics run,
    serial, 14 of them), the mutants about 0.32 s each. The runner runs tests about 2.2 times
    slower (night #12's copy run, 0.218 s a test, against 0.100 s), which puts a capped night's
    setup near 60 minutes and its 1,301 mutants near 15: `NIGHT_CAP` is 20 for that.
- **The budget** is the one setting, `MUTATION_BUDGET_MINUTES` (120): what it does not reach is
  named in the summary, and its results so far are kept. The mutate step WRITES bytecode:
  mutmut's copy of a module holds every mutant of it (`config_check.py`: 2168 mutants, 7.5 MB,
  7.7 s to compile), and a test's child process recompiled it each time, so one survivor's tests
  took 107 s, not 7.
- **The record** is kept in the Actions cache after every night whose results stand: the commit
  covered and, per function still unfinished or holding an open survivor, a hash of its text and
  every result so far (C769). While a function's text is unchanged, the next night runs only its
  mutants not yet checked and its open survivors, by name (mutmut numbers a function's mutants
  from its text, with mutmut pinned), and merges the rest; a function whose text changed starts
  afresh. So a large function is finished across nights, and an open survivor is run again
  every night until a test kills it or a person lists it as equivalent. Walked 2026-10-14: a
  night cut by its budget after 2 of 56 mutants, then a night from its record that ran exactly
  the other 54 and gave the same table as one whole night.
- **What a mutant changes** (the operator's rule, 2026-10-14, so the night's red means
  something), decided from mutmut's own copy of the module before anything runs, by parsing
  each mutant against the original (`scripts/nmas_mutation.py`, `classify`):
  - **logging:** the change lies inside a logging call's arguments (`log.debug(...)` and its
    kin, continuation lines included). Never run, never counted (PIT's default). One rule in
    one place, not a pragma per line; mutmut's own `do_not_mutate_patterns` matches single
    lines and would miss a call's continuation lines, or hit an identical line elsewhere.
  - **MESSAGE:** the change is confined to the text of a string literal that holds whitespace
    (words a person reads), and that text holds no word-like string the module compares with
    (`==`, `in`, `startswith`: config_check decides by `startswith("no golden")`, so its "no
    golden: …" note is VERDICT).
  - **VERDICT:** everything else: a check's name or level, pass or fail, whom a result blames
    (a device, a file), a condition, a value's type, an expression inside an f-string; and
    whatever the rule cannot decide.
- **It fails** when an open VERDICT survivor remains (a mutant no test killed, "no tests"
  included, not in `tests/mutation_equivalent.py`), or when the measurement or the run broke
  (the canary, the scope, mutmut's own exit 1: its setup or the clean run of the tests on
  unmutated code). MESSAGE survivors are listed and counted in their own section and kept open
  in the record, re-run each night, and never turn the night red. Nothing changed and nothing
  kept: green, "Nothing to mutate".
- **Its first walk** (the laptop, 2026-10-14, the night's own steps over the two Lab 7 seam
  commits, f40c9da6 and 1dc672ea): 56 mutants of `reachability.probe` and
  `monitoring_profile.tcp_accepts`. Five real survivors, now killed (each probe's bound, the
  address ping is asked about, a device answering in under a millisecond, an IPv6 address's
  own colons), and 16 equivalents listed; then 0 new survivors, the night green. The walk is
  also where two rules came from: loopback brought up in the namespace (without it a test's
  own listener read "Network is unreachable" and mutmut exited 1), and one mutant at a time.

**Reading the summary:** the coverage map it selected by (run, commit, date; or none, and why),
the canary's line (all its mutants killed: the measurement works), the
scope's (how many mutants ran, all of the planned functions, and how many functions the record
carried in, and how many logging mutants were never run), how the tests were chosen (by the
map, or by tonight's refresh, each stale function with its reason, the refresh's exit, time and
any test that failed in it, and each function deferred) and the children
measured (and each test that was not), the functions the cap left waiting, a table per function (mutants,
killed, survived VERDICT, survived MESSAGE, known equivalents; the score, killed over the
mutants a test could kill; and the VERDICT score, killed over killed and VERDICT survivors),
then the open VERDICT survivors with their line before and after (each one keeps the night
failing; "no test reached it" marks one no test ran; "STALE MAP" one found under a stale
selection, never added to the debt list), the open MESSAGE survivors (listed,
never failing), the known equivalents with their reasons, what the budget left (kept, resumed next night),
and any function mutmut made no mutant of (nothing in it was tested that night). The artifact
`mutation-report` holds `report.json` (every mutant's status), `run.json` (each mutmut run's
exit, the tests that start a child) and the plan.

**How to triage a survivor:** read its diff (the summary's lines, or `mutmut show <name>`). If
some behaviour a person relies on changed and no test failed, write the test that pins it (a
docstring naming the behaviour) and run the mutant again to see it killed. If no behaviour can
observe the change, add it BY HAND to `tests/mutation_equivalent.py` with the function, the line
before and after, and a one-line reason; an entry is matched by those, never by mutmut's
number, which moves when the function changes. Never chase an equivalent mutant with a test.

**To run a night on the laptop:** install `requirements-mutation.txt` `--no-deps` into its own
folder and put it on `PYTHONPATH`, then run the workflow's three steps: `scripts/nmas-mutation
plan --state <state.json> --head <sha> --out mutation-out [--also path::qualname] [--reach
<drill-down> --reach-commit <its sha> --reach-run <its run> --reach-date <its date>]
[--stale-map defer]` (the drill-down: `scripts/nmas-ci-log run <coverage nightly run>
--artifact coverage-drilldown --out <dir>`; without `--stale-map defer` a stale function's map
is refreshed, the whole suite run once, 9 to 14 minutes here),
`scripts/nmas-mutation run --out mutation-out` inside `unshare -rn` with `ip link set lo up` (as
the workflow), and `scripts/nmas-mutation report --plan mutation-out/plan.json --summary <file>
--state-out <next.json> --mutmut-exit <its exit>`. Run it in a copy of the tree when you will
edit while it runs: each mutmut run copies `tests/` afresh, so an edit mid-night mixes old and
new tests in one measurement. Its working files (`setup.cfg`, `mutants/`, `mutation-out/`) are
gitignored. The tool's own tests are `tests/test_nmas_mutation.py` (on mutmut's real output
captured in `tests/fixtures/mutation/`) and the canary's `tests/test_mutation_canary.py`.

**A walk before a GitHub night walks THAT night.** The first GitHub night (2026-10-14, a
dispatch over 68c86aba..371a5604) failed in mutmut's clean run on a test no laptop night had
selected: `test_config_read` found 0 of its 9 configs, because in mutmut's copy (`mutants/`, a
folder the checkout ignores) `git ls-files` answered for the checkout around it and every scan
over `tests.source_index.tracked()` saw nothing. The laptop nights had passed only because they
planned other functions. So:
- **Plan what the runner will plan:** the same record (none on a first night, whose base is
  `first_base`, the commit that added the workflow), the same `--head`, the same `--also`. The
  plan's lines (`base … head …: N function(s) … M test file(s)`) must match the run's.
- **Stand the tests on what the runner gives them:** PostgreSQL 18's libraries on
  `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and `NMAS_REQUIRE_PG=1` (the gate's), promtool, and a network namespace.
  The workflow takes each setup step from ci.yml's test job (`TestTheNightStandsOnCIsSetup`
  holds the two to the same steps).
- **The namespace:** the runner lifts Ubuntu's restriction in its own step
  (`kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0`), so its `unshare -rn` succeeds. A laptop
  walk needs a shell that can make one too: VS Code's terminal (the `nmas-test` profile above
  covers only that script, and a walk calls `unshare` itself). A shell started by
  `systemd-run --user` is plain `unconfined`, as
  an ordinary terminal is: it reproduces an operator's refused run, not the runner, and the
  walk stops there at `unshare` (measured 2026-10-14).
- **A failed setup or clean run says why in the summary:** `nmas-mutation run` keeps each
  mutmut run's whole output (`mutation-out/mutmut-run-<n>.log`, in the report's artifact) and
  the summary quotes its FAILED and error lines (`failure_excerpt`).
- **Only the planned functions reach mutmut** (`plan --fence`, C778): mutmut mutates every
  function of a file it is given, so the plan fences each other function and class of a planned
  module off with mutmut's own pragma, in place, in the night's own checkout (a laptop walk runs
  it in a clone; it refuses a module with uncommitted changes). Unfenced, two changed functions
  of `modules/pipeline.py` made 5,030 mutants of 56 functions and a 50.78 MB copy, the clean run
  took 5.7 s a test, and a scan of an unplanned function's source failed; fenced, 77 mutants of
  the 2, 0.24 MB.
- **A test that fails in mutmut's copy itself is not run that night, and is named** (C779): a
  scan of a planned module's definitions meets mutmut's generated copies of the planned
  functions and fails with no mutant active, so it cannot tell a mutant from the original. When
  mutmut's first run fails, the night's tests run once in the copy (no stop at the first
  failure); each that fails there is deselected, the summary lists it, and mutmut runs again.
  Measured each night: the walk of 2026-10-14 found 2 of 2,725.
- **No bulk moves to the debt list (the operator, 2026-11-05, C2551).**
  - A debt-list addition needs the operator's approval and its `Test-Weakened` trailer, entry by
    entry.
  - A mutant marked equivalent carries its own one-line reason why the change cannot be
    observed, sent to the operator in batches.
  - A night's survivors are registered on their first failure (`scripts/nmas-scheduled-failures`,
    C2552) and killed by a campaign the operator directs.
- **Known debt** (`tests/mutation_debt.json`; the operator, 2026-10-14). Code that was only
  moved arrives with hundreds of survivors at once (C781: the AI family's shared pieces, never
  tested directly), and a night red for weeks says nothing new. Like the coverage ratchet's
  baseline, the debt list holds each known open VERDICT survivor, by function and its two
  lines, with the reason it was accepted, and each function's path, qualname and text hash.
  It grows only by `scripts/nmas-mutation debt add --from-report <a night's report.json>
  --reason "…"` (a night's report comes from its `mutation-report` artifact: `scripts/nmas-ci-log
  run <id> --artifact mutation-report --out <dir>`); killing a survivor shrinks it (its entry
  is removed by hand). `TestTheDebt` refuses an entry for a function that no longer exists, or
  one without a reason. A night is red only on a VERDICT survivor NOT on the list, on the list
  having grown since the last night's record (red once: an addition is seen), or on a broken
  canary or scope; the summary reports the debt every night (its size, its change since the
  last night, the survivors met, the functions holding most) and leads with **"N known, M
  new"**. **Known debt is not run again while its function's text is the one it was listed
  at** (the operator, 2026-10-14): only a function's unchecked mutants run, one with none left
  is not planned, and the summary names it ("Known debt not run again"); the budget goes to
  what is unchecked or changed. **"New" is decided by text:** an entry counts only at the hash
  its function was listed at, so a survivor in code changed afterwards is new and turns the
  night red. **The baseline sweep** (`tests/mutation_sweep.json`, the operator's approval for
  night #4's 20 left-over functions only): a survivor found finishing them, still at their
  listed text, is reported as found finishing the sweep, never failing the night, and added
  with `debt add --reason "baseline sweep of moved code"`, which adds only those; such entries
  are not counted as the list growing. Once the sweep's functions are finished, or changed, it
  holds nothing a night can find.
- **Moved, not changed**: a function whose text hash the record or the debt list already holds
  under another name is moved. The record's results for it carry over, renamed (the same text
  makes the same mutants, numbered the same), and only what was left or open runs; one the
  record finished (the record keeps every finished function's hash) or one on the debt list is
  not mutated again. The summary lists them apart.
- **A function only moved** (another module's function of the same name, its text unchanged at
  the base) is named as moved in the plan and the summary, and mutated in full: the record keys
  a function by path and name, and the tests that reach it moved with it, so its old results
  are not carried.

## Size and organisation

*Dated: measured 2026-09-26. Today's figures come from the coverage tool's report (above, and
each CI run's job summary): on 2026-10-14, 512 test files and 8,990 test functions.*

- **3,942 tests in 137 files** (median 19 per file). They come from 3,552 test
  functions, some run with several inputs.
- Organised by **property, not by module.** Most files are named for what must
  stay true: `test_credential_never_changes_on_deploy`,
  `test_reads_write_nothing`, `test_server_reads_nothing_the_form_cannot_send`.
- **Nothing touches a live network, device, or data store.** Every SSH, NETCONF
  and HTTP call is mocked. The store rule is enforced, not assumed: the suite
  runs on a temporary directory, and a run FAILS if the checkout's `data/`
  changes at all (see *The suite had never run clean anywhere*, below).
- CI runs it on every push, on the deployment host's exact package versions
  (`requirements.lock`, generated on the host), in about 4 minutes including
  coverage.

## Where the weight sits

| Area | Tests | Share |
|---|---|---|
| Deploy path: plan, confirm by hash, merge-only push, verify, rollback | 574 | 14.6% |
| Intent and templates: parse, render, round-trip, approval, editing | 552 | 14.0% |
| Credentials: rotation, persistence to boot files, break-glass | 480 | 12.2% |
| Onboarding and retirement | 469 | 11.9% |
| Golden repository and history: commits, restore, remote | 441 | 11.2% |
| Rules about the code and the test harness itself | 353 | 9.0% |
| NetBox safety and provenance | 337 | 8.5% |
| Monitoring and health: drift, freshness, heartbeat, jobs | 325 | 8.2% |
| Identity, gates, secrets, redaction | 309 | 7.8% |
| Settings | 102 | 2.6% |

The single heaviest files are credential rotation (194 tests), deploy safety
(137) and NetBox update provenance (103). Almost a tenth of the suite checks the
code and the harness rather than the product: every script reaches its own
imports, no module computes the data path itself, no removed function is still
called, CI can read no other repository.

## Negative controls: 180 that run every time, ~330 that ran once

This is the number that separates this suite from one that merely runs code. A
test with a control that provably fails when its property is removed is a
different artefact from an assertion that happens to pass. There are two kinds,
and they must never be added together.

- **About 180 built-in controls and floors, in 72 of the 137 files, run on
  every execution.** These are tests that prove the check CAN see the case:
  - "the scan finds the population";
  - "a real tag change is still recorded", beside "an unchanged one is not";
  - "the fallback still uses a real enable secret".

  Counted by name and docstring; 11 of a random 12 were genuine.
- **About 330 mutation controls ran once, at commit time, and are NOT
  re-verified.** Before a commit, the property a test protects was removed from
  the code (a guard deleted, a comparison inverted, a branch forced), and the
  test was shown to FAIL, not crash, then the code was restored. They are
  counted from the numbers stated in 86 commit messages. They are not linked to
  their tests in a machine-readable way, and nothing re-runs them.

**The natural extension is mutation testing** (for example `mutmut`), which
would make the second kind repeatable. It is recorded, not scoped.

Two rules came out of running the controls, both recorded in the project's
rules:
- **A control that fires by CRASHING proves nothing.** A syntax error makes
  every test fail. A valid control fails the tests aimed at its property, with
  no collection errors.
- **A control that PASSES is either a missing test or a broken control.**
  Telling which is the work.

## The kinds of property the tests assert

Classified from test names, so read the shares as approximate:

| Kind | Approx. share | Example |
|---|---|---|
| A refusal happens | 12% | a credential rotation still refuses when the account's form changed |
| A scan has a floor; a count has its denominator | 8% | every mutating route is declared, and the scan must find at least 115 |
| A refusal names its cause and both operands | 7% | a missing lab directory is reported as local, not remote |
| A secret never leaks and is stored safely | 6% | files are created owner-only; masked values never reach a comparison |
| It is recorded or audited | 5% | a golden commit carries its manifest; a terminal open is one audit row |
| Output is exact, or round-trips faithfully | 4% | a device's config re-renders to itself |
| A payload field is drawn on screen | 4% | the shipped JavaScript, executed against the real endpoint's payload |
| Order and sequence | 4% | promotion last; rollback exempt from the dangerous-line gate |
| Idempotent and stable, no churn | 2% | a repeat NetBox sync records nothing |
| Plain behaviour: this input, that output | 49% | |

### Performance: work and growth, never wall-clock (the operator, 2026-10-25)

A performance test asserts on the WORK done, counted (calls made, questions asked, rows built,
nodes a walk expands, devices reached), or on its GROWTH from N to 10N (the work about 10x for
a linear path, the same for one that must not grow; if a time must be compared, the ratio of
the two times under about 15x, never either time alone), never on an absolute time. Why: CI
#1177 failed on tests/test_network_model.py's scale tests, a 900-device build of 0.569 s on
the hosted runner against a 0.4 s bound measured on the laptop, and the subgraph's 0.0142 s
against 0.01 s; the fix-forward that only raised the bounds (C1741) would fail again on a
slower runner, and a bound loose enough never to fail would not catch a quadratic step. A work
count fails on the defect (a walk that visits every node, a question per device, a pass per
pair) on any machine, and passes on every runner otherwise. Converted so far:
`test_network_model.py` (`TestScale`: one pass per device and edges exactly 10x from 90 to
900; one node expanded for a one-hop subgraph at both sizes) and
`test_evidence_pack_context.py` (a capture's four questions and expanded nodes the same at 90
and 900, its kept overlay the same while the read holds ten times as much). **It does not
change timeouts:** a process's, a test's or the suite's bound is still about 2.5x a measured
time (CLAUDE.md, "Bounds are about 2.5x a measured time"; `NMAS_TEST_TIMEOUT`, CI's step and
job bounds), because a bound there stops a hang, not a slow machine.

### AI prompt versions: adoption is relative, done is absolute (the operator, 2026-10-26)

A prompt version's recorded cases (`tests/fixtures/ai_cases/`) are measured five runs a case
with `scripts/nmas-nl-cases` (Ask in words) or `scripts/nmas-pack-replay` (Explain), recorded
as an evaluation, never a person (C1784), the stale check first, the date-relative cases at
their own frozen "now".
- **Reliability decides, not consistency** (the operator, 2026-10-27, as the rule's owner).
  Consistency as first defined rewarded being consistently wrong: feature 7's case 33, Sonnet
  wrong in 10 of 10 runs, counted as consistent, while Haiku, right in 5 of 10, counted as
  inconsistent. **A case is reliable when it is correct in every run; reliability is the share
  of cases that are.** A consistently wrong case counts against it. Applied symmetrically to
  every model and every version. Cost: none at the run, only the scoring. Prevents: adopting
  or keeping a version because it repeats a wrong answer.
- **Adoption is relative.** A candidate replaces the current version when no case the current
  version passes reliably becomes unreliable under it, and its overall reliability does not
  drop. Cases the current version fails are not protected. Both are measured on the main set
  and on a blind held-out set, written before any run by someone who saw neither the prompts
  nor any result.
- **A blind set decides once.** The next version is measured on a new one written the same
  way.
- **Done is absolute:** 11.1's floor applied to reliability, 95% (Translator, Decision-maker)
  or 90% (Analyst; Explain).
- **A candidate that passes adoption but not the floor goes live,** and the feature stays not
  done until a later version meets the floor.
- **Consistency is still reported, beside reliability, and decides nothing.** It compares the
  card's fields only (PHASE8_PLAN section 6's table: for Ask in words, the builder's query
  model whole; a question back or a refusal on its outcome), never the prose, and is never
  redefined to pass.
- **A run refused before it was sent fails twice** (the operator, 2026-10-26, from metrics v9:
  two cases refused over the prompt budget in all five runs were counted as agreeing). A
  request Mercury refused before sending it (over the prompt budget, over a cap) is a failed
  run for pass, reliability and consistency. A case holding one is never reliable or
  consistent, five identical refusals included. Mercury's own answer made with no call is an outcome, not a refusal:
  its guidance on a question no metric matches, and its own question back (logs v4's
  ambiguous role).
- **Statistics, while the sprint rules are active** (the operator, 2026-10-27):
  - held-out sets grow to about 30 cases, written blind, the existing ones extended;
  - adoption and done decisions take 10 runs a case;
  - reliability and consistency are reported with their cases and runs beside them.
- **Cost to performance** (the operator, 2026-10-27):
  - Among candidates (model, prompt version, context level) that pass the adoption bar and meet
    the done floor, the one with the lowest cost per successful answer is adopted. A dearer one
    only when it alone meets the bars, its extra cost said.
  - The smallest model that meets the floor per task. Larger models are measurement ceilings.
  - Every measurement reports cost per call and cost per successful answer beside pass and
    consistency, and flags a version whose cost rose without a gain the bars count.
- **The rule's record:** PHASE8_PLAN 15.12.

## What is NOT tested

This is distinct from code that simply did not run. Line coverage is 57%
overall, and the low figures sit mostly in code being cut or rebuilt (the agent
15%, the old configure tab 5%, topology 6%, the collectors 14-21%), while
`modules/nsot`, the core that reaches devices, is at 87.8%. What follows is
untested in code that STAYS.

1. **The boundary with real devices and services.** Every SSH, NETCONF and
   HTTP call is mocked, and coverage shows the consequence:
   - **`pipeline.py` (67%)**, which every deploy runs: its stages that touch a
     device run almost none of their own statements (pre/post snapshot, the
     push, the NetBox query).
   - **`netbox_client.py` (35%)**: the importer's config parsers are 72 of 73
     statements untested, and the sync and removal bodies about 98%. What IS
     heavily tested there is the write chokepoints (the gate, provenance, the
     modification recorder).
   - **`credential_rotation.py` (81%)**: the live read of a device's user line
     is untested.

   The tests prove the PROGRAM is correct (what will be sent, in what order,
   under which refusals). They cannot prove a device ACCEPTS it. **The project
   has a measured count of the difference: 15 defects found by walking the
   onboarding path live that the suite missed** (docs/PHASE2_DHCP.md, section
   10), every one in a seam between two individually tested halves.
2. **The browser.** Render functions run in an embedded JavaScript engine
   against real payloads. Event handling, the order of fetches, and real DOM
   behaviour are covered only by source scans.
   **"Drawn" is where the mechanised checks stop** (the operator, C138,
   2026-09-28). The payload-to-render and results checks prove a field
   reaches a renderer and lands in the markup. They cannot prove a person can
   SEE it: eight code blocks full of the import's failures rendered as light
   text on a near-white block, every check passing. No contrast check is
   built, deliberately: it would test the stylesheet, not the reading. The
   only detector for "drawn and unreadable" is somebody looking at the
   screen, which is why a real run (R1, R2, C70) belongs to every stage and
   is not a formality.
3. **The host.** systemd units and timers, file ownership, and the lab-host
   shell scripts (partly: one script's case block runs under bash).
4. **Concurrency beyond settings writes.** Nothing tests two simultaneous
   deploys or restores, drift racing a deploy, or the repository lock across
   processes (it is a lock within one process).
5. **Anything outside a fixture.** Parsers and round-trips are proven on nine
   real captured configs and whatever those contain.
6. **A test made weaker without being deleted, skipped or bounded looser.**
   `scripts/nmas-test-weakening-check` (2026-10-18) refuses a commit that deletes a
   test, adds a skip, xfail or `pragma: no cover`, moves a declared ratchet
   (tests/ratchet_lists.py) the wrong way, or loosens a numeric bound in an
   assert, unless a `Test-Weakened:` trailer names it with a register row. It
   does NOT see: an assertion made weaker (an `==` become `in`, a check removed
   from a body, a bound's expression rewritten so the old and new bounds are
   not the same comparison); a test renamed AND edited (it is reported as
   deleted, the edit itself unseen); a parametrize case removed; a new test
   born skipped, or a new helper's skip reached by existing tests; a ratchet
   held anywhere but a registered module-level literal or an assert in tests/
   (a bound in an `if`, a count compared in a helper, a ceiling compared in
   another module: tests/test_large_fleets.py's `if len(shown) > LIMIT` and
   tests/test_signed_off_screens.py's `<= R.UNSIGNED_CEILING` are reached
   only because `LIMIT` and `UNSIGNED_CEILING` themselves are registered); an
   exclusion table whose name carries none of the registry's stems and whose
   comment does not say it only shrinks (`DECLARED`, `NOT_AN_OPERATION`,
   `NOT_FROM_THE_FORM`, `SCANNED`, `SURVEYED` and others: whether each is a
   ratchet is the operator's call); `pragma: no cover` in a file without the
   `.py` suffix (the scripts under scripts/); and a coverage exclusion added
   to a configuration file. The rule holds these; only a reader enforces them.

## Fidelity to the signed-off boards (C650, 2026-10-10)

The browser tests check behaviour: a control does what it says, a region redraws, a page
fits its width. None of them says whether the screen looks like the board it was signed off
from, and P.11's Topology shipped without its ports and neighbourship states because of that.
So every board-built screen has a fidelity step:

1. **Shoot the board and the page side by side.** `tests/test_board_shots.py` renders the
   board's own file (a copy of the mockups canvas's `project/` folder, read with the Artifact
   tool) and the page as built, fed from real captures, in the same headless Firefox, at the
   board's width, at 1280 and at phone width. It runs only when asked:
   `NMAS_BOARD_SHOTS=<out folder> NMAS_BOARDS_DIR=<the boards> scripts/nmas-test
   --allow-unconfined tests/test_board_shots.py`. Firefox's narrowest window is 488 CSS px,
   so a phone shot holds the page to a 390 px column; the phone's media rules apply to both.
2. **Compare region by region** and write `docs/fidelity/<screen>.md`: each region's verdict,
   **same**, **deviation** (each one a line in docs/STANDING_APPROVAL_LOG.md, named in the
   record) or **later** (a later step, named), the templates compared and their sha256.
3. **`tests/test_board_fidelity.py` holds it:** every signed-off screen has a record or is on
   its UNCHECKED list (which only shrinks); a record whose templates changed since it was
   written fails, printing the new hash, so a changed screen is compared again before the
   record is.

## The suite had never run clean anywhere (found 2026-09-26)

The first run from a pristine checkout gave **5 failures and 19 errors**,
every one passing in the development checkout:
- **Tests wrote into the live `data/` directory.** The guard meant to stop
  that looked only for NEW paths, so directories left behind by earlier runs
  hid it.
- **Four tests had never tested their property.** Their patch missed its
  target, and they passed by reading the developer's own settings file.

Until then "N passed" had partly been a statement about one machine. The fixes:
- one owner of the data path, and a temporary store for every run;
- a run that fails if the real store changes, even by a file created and
  deleted;
- importing the application starts no services;
- CI on a clean runner, with the host's versions.

Two product defects surfaced the same way: a deploy PLAN and an onboarding
PLAN, both reads, were creating directories.

## Running it

```bash
scripts/nmas-test                 # confined: no process the suite starts can reach a network
scripts/nmas-test tests/test_x.py -k name
```

`scripts/nmas-test` runs pytest in a loopback-only network namespace (C46).
The first line says `network: CONFINED`, and the run stops if that is not
measured to hold. Plain `pytest` still works: its header says `NOT CONFINED`,
and the test process itself still refuses any non-loopback connect. The
deployment host cannot make the namespace (AppArmor), so `--offline` there
runs unconfined and says so in its verdict.

Every process a test starts is also refused a network **by construction**,
on every machine including the host: a wrapper on `subprocess.Popen` gives
each child a `sitecustomize` (Python), refusing shims for `ssh`, `curl`,
`rsync` and the rest, and local-only git, and any attempt fails the test that
made it, by name (C46).

`requirements-test.txt` pins the test tools the host AND CI install
(`pytest-xdist`): the runner that decides test order must be one version.

### From an ordinary terminal (Ubuntu 24.04)

**The interpreter.** With no `PYTHON` given, `scripts/nmas-test` runs CI's environment,
`~/.local/share/nmas-py312/bin/python` (built once by `scripts/nmas-ci-env`, the next section).
Without that environment, it runs `python3` only if that is the version `ci.yml` pins, and
otherwise refuses, naming both versions and the command that builds the right one. Its second
line names the interpreter it ran. `PYTHON=<python>` still chooses one (the gate and
`nmas-deploy` pass theirs), and that line says when it is not CI's version. A terminal whose
`python3` is 3.14 used to run the suite on 3.14 without a word (the operator, 2026-10-14).

**The namespace.** From a GNOME Terminal the run refuses with `no network namespace can be
made here: unshare: write failed /proc/self/uid_map: Operation not permitted`, while the
same command in VS Code's terminal runs confined. The cause, measured 2026-10-14:
- Ubuntu 24.04 sets `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1`. A process with the
  AppArmor label `unconfined` that makes a user namespace gets one without capabilities, so
  `unshare -rn` cannot write its uid map.
- VS Code's own profile (`/etc/apparmor.d/code`: `profile vscode … flags=(unconfined) {
  userns, }`) grants user namespaces, and everything VS Code starts inherits the label
  `vscode (unconfined)`, its integrated terminal included. A GNOME Terminal's shell is plain
  `unconfined`.
- Reproduced without changing anything: `systemd-run --user --wait --pipe bash -c 'unshare
  -rn true'` (label `unconfined`) fails with the same message; the same command from VS
  Code's terminal succeeds.

Two ways to run it confined, neither of them `--allow-unconfined`:
1. **Nothing installed:** run it in VS Code's integrated terminal (Terminal › New Terminal).
2. **Any terminal: a profile like VS Code's, for this script.** It is a system change, so it
   is the operator's to run (with `sudo`), once per checkout path. Replace `<checkout>` with the
   checkout's absolute path:

   ```bash
   sudo tee /etc/apparmor.d/nmas-test > /dev/null <<'EOF'
   # Gives scripts/nmas-test, and what it starts, user namespaces, as VS Code's profile does.
   abi <abi/5.0>,
   include <tunables/global>

   profile nmas-test <checkout>/scripts/nmas-test flags=(unconfined) {
     userns,
     include if exists <local/nmas-test>
   }
   EOF
   sudo apparmor_parser -r /etc/apparmor.d/nmas-test
   ```

   PASS: `sudo aa-status | grep nmas-test` lists the profile, and `scripts/nmas-test
   tests/test_claude_md.py` from a GNOME Terminal prints `nmas-test: network: CONFINED`,
   then the interpreter line, then the tests. Undo: `sudo apparmor_parser -R
   /etc/apparmor.d/nmas-test && sudo rm /etc/apparmor.d/nmas-test`.

   What it grants: anything run through that one path may make user namespaces, which VS
   Code already grants everything it starts. The script lives in a folder the operator can
   write, so the profile gives the operator nothing they could not already get by opening VS
   Code; it widens nothing for another user. The profile names the script's own path, the path a
   person executes; that AppArmor attaches it to a `#!` script there is NOT yet measured on
   this laptop, because the agent changes no system setting. If `aa-status` lists the profile but the run still
   refuses, the attachment did not take; say so, and the profile goes on a root-owned copy of
   `unshare` that the script calls instead.

### CI's interpreter here

**The records tests' real PostgreSQL (Phase 4, option a).** `tests/pg_instance.py` starts a
throwaway server inside the suite's namespace from unpacked binaries. CI installs `libpq5` and
the server's libraries and unpacks `postgresql-18` from PGDG (the workflow's PostgreSQL step) and sets
`NMAS_REQUIRE_PG=1`, so a missing libpq or server FAILS the job. The gate sets it too and puts
`~/.local/share/nmas-pg`'s libpq on the suite's library path itself, so a laptop without them
fails the gate, naming why; a bare `scripts/nmas-test` skips them with their reason. Unpack
the same once, without root:

```bash
d=$(mktemp -d) && cd "$d" && apt-get download postgresql-18 libpq5 \
  && for f in *.deb; do dpkg -x "$f" ~/.local/share/nmas-pg; done \
  && ln -sf libpq.so.5 ~/.local/share/nmas-pg/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libpq.so
# The gate adds it; for a bare run: LD_LIBRARY_PATH=~/.local/share/nmas-pg/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu
```

A green run on the development laptop's Python (3.14) says nothing about CI's
(3.12.3, with the host's pinned packages): that gap is a standing source of
CI-only failures (the operator, 2026-10-01, C270). The pre-push gate runs CI's
own command in an environment that IS CI's:

```bash
# Once: CI's exact interpreter, without root. A python-build-standalone release
# of the version ci.yml pins, checked against that release's SHA256SUMS before
# it is unpacked; then the venv with CI's three requirement files, --no-deps.
scripts/nmas-ci-env ~/.local/opt/cpython-3.12.3/bin/python3

# The gate (scripts/nmas-gate runs exactly this, for each of CI's four jobs, all four at
# once): CI's command, its workers from the memory available now (below; never more than
# CI's `-n auto` on a 4-vCPU hosted runner, the -n 4 written here), coverage on and measured
# by tier, confined, the job's shard of the files (scripts/nmas-shards: browser1, browser2, a,
# b); then CI's coverage ratchet over the four (step 4b, C808).
D=~/.local/share/nmas-browser
PY=~/.local/share/nmas-py312/bin/python
M=$(mktemp -d); mkdir "$M/tiers"
for S in browser1 browser2 a b; do
  PATH=$D:$D/firefox:$PATH PYTHON=$PY COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon NMAS_COVERAGE_TIERS=1 \
    COVERAGE_FILE=$M/.coverage.$S NMAS_TEST_TIERS=$M/tiers \
    NMAS_TEST_TIMEOUT=740 scripts/nmas-test -q -p no:cacheprovider -n 4 \
    --cov=modules --cov=routes --cov=app --cov-report= -rEfs $($PY scripts/nmas-shards $S) &
done; wait
$PY -m coverage combine --keep --data-file=$M/.coverage $M/.coverage.*
$PY scripts/nmas-coverage report --data $M/.coverage --tiers $M/tiers --check
```

CI runs the suite as four jobs at once (2026-10-03; four since C614, when the files that start
a real browser weighed 40% of the suite), each about a quarter of the measured work: the two
browser jobs share every file that starts a real browser, then all four share the rest, and
the files are placed by `tests/shard_weights.json` (each file's seconds from a
`--durations=0` run, plus about 17 ms a test). Measure again and rewrite the weights when
`test_ci_shards.py` says the map has gone stale.

`nmas-ci-env` refuses an interpreter whose version is not the one `ci.yml`
pins, so a stale environment cannot pass for CI's. `tests/test_nmas_gate.py` reads CI's test
command from `ci.yml` and holds the gate's to every argument of it.

### The browser tests

CI's runner has a Firefox that starts inside the loopback namespace, so in CI the browser tests
run IN the confined, parallel suite, after whatever else their worker ran. The laptop's snap
Firefox cannot start there, so until 2026-10-03 they skipped in the gate's suite and ran only
in a separate clean process: CI was red for five commits (ca52963 to 64d4377) on a failure no
local run could meet, a Socket.IO test client earlier in the same worker that had diverted the
app server's packets (now restored after every test, `tests/conftest.py`). The gate now puts a
Mozilla build of Firefox and geckodriver first on PATH and REFUSES a suite in which any browser
test skipped. Once, without root:

```bash
D=~/.local/share/nmas-browser; mkdir -p $D && cd $D
curl -sSfLO https://ftp.mozilla.org/pub/firefox/releases/156.0.1/linux-x86_64/en-US/firefox-156.0.1.tar.xz
tar xf firefox-156.0.1.tar.xz
curl -sSfL https://github.com/mozilla/geckodriver/releases/download/v0.36.0/geckodriver-v0.36.0-linux64.tar.gz | tar xz
```

The version is the laptop's own snap Firefox's; CI's is in each run's `nmas-env-facts` notice.

**A browser session keeps everything in its own folder (C391, C392).** Its downloads, its
profile and (for a non-snap Firefox) its HOME are inside a folder named for the run, removed when
the session ends, including a session that could not start. The session end fails a run that
left anything new in the person's download folder, or a session folder behind, naming each (a
file downloaded by hand during a run is named too). Before 2026-10-03 the export tests' records
landed in the laptop's Downloads, and every confined process left a geckodriver running.

**The browser tests load the page the app serves; the host's people may not (C389).** A proxy
in front of the host can rewrite the page on the way (on 2026-10-03 one injected an email
decoder and an analytics beacon), and then what a person sees is not what any test checked.
Two defences, each tested: every HTML answer carries `Cache-Control: no-transform`, and every
v2 page checks itself on load (`nmas_v2.js`, `injectedScripts`), saying at its top which
scripts the tool did not send. A notice "This page arrived changed" on the host means the
tests' page and the person's differ until the proxy stops.

## Reproducing these numbers

```bash
python -m pytest --collect-only -q | grep -c '::'                  # tests
python -m pytest --cov=modules --cov=routes --cov=app --cov-report=term
```
The clusters, control counts and property kinds were computed by scripts over
the collected test list, test ASTs and `git log`. The figures above are from
2026-09-26 and will drift.

## The per-file test table and the runner's notes (moved from CLAUDE.md on 2026-10-02)

CLAUDE.md's Tests section, moved verbatim. The per-file table is kept here: add a
row for a new test file in this table, not in CLAUDE.md.

**Hook tests** (`test_claude_*_hook.py`): a hook test's refused-form list is named REFUSED or
REFUSED_<kind>. The scan in tests/test_test_weakening_check.py
(`TestEveryHookTestsRefusedFormsGrow`) finds it by that name and requires it to be declared
`grows` in tests/ratchet_lists.py.

### Tests

```bash
scripts/nmas-test         # the suite, confined to loopback (C46); args go to pytest
scripts/nmas-test -n auto # in parallel: ONLY where pytest-xdist is installed
pytest                    # unconfined; says so in its header
pytest tests/test_netbox_write_gate.py -v
```

**Where each way runs** (2026-09-28): pytest-xdist 3.8.0 (execnet 2.1.2) is
installed on the deployment host, in CI, and now on the development laptop, so
all three schedule tests the same way (C43's class is a test depending on what
ran before it). **Why the laptop lacked it:** its Python is the system 3.14,
marked `EXTERNALLY-MANAGED` (PEP 668), so `pip install` refuses. It went into
the user site instead, where pytest itself already was
(`pip install --user --break-system-packages --no-deps pytest-xdist==3.8.0
execnet==2.1.2`: `~/.local` only, never the system). `apt install
python3-pytest-xdist` (Ubuntu's 3.8.0) is the other route and needs sudo.
Measured on the laptop: 5025 passed in **42 s** with `-n auto` (24 cores)
against **121 s** serial.

**The bounds come from measurements, and a bound that fires names what was
running** (the operator, 2026-09-28). `scripts/nmas-test` stops the run at
`NMAS_TEST_TIMEOUT` (300 s, 2.5x the serial run) and prints the test each
process was running and every thread's stack (`tests/conftest.py` records it
per process; `tests/test_suite_bound.py` drives a real hang).
`faulthandler_timeout = 120` in `pytest.ini` dumps one slow test's stack without stopping
the run: 45 s until 2026-10-14, when the dump itself was found taking xdist workers down
(C647: a browser test past 45 s under the gate's load, its worker's output cut mid-dump,
three times). 120 s is about 2.5x that test's loaded time. CI's tests step overrides it
with `-o faulthandler_timeout=270` (C2036, 2026-10-28): test_v2_context_is_drawn's module setup,
the walk of every v2 page, measured 108.6 s on the runner (#1266) and passed 120 s twice in
the docs shard (#1267); 270 s is 2.5x the 108.6 s. The coverage nightly's is 450 s (C1616,
the C tracer). CI's tests step is bound at 1470 s
and its job at 26 min (2.5x the 587 s step measured in run #752 with the per-test measurement;
`timeout-minutes` in the workflow); each of the gate's shards is bound at 740 s at `-n 4`,
scaled with its workers (2960 s at `-n 1`: a shard's time goes as 1/n; `suite_bound` in
`scripts/nmas-gate`).

**Workers from the memory available now; one full-suite run at a time** (the operator,
2026-10-19: the laptop's RAM ran out with the gate's four shards at `-n 4` and two agents'
runs beside them, swap 8 of 8 GiB). `scripts/nmas-workers` measures MemAvailable before each
run and allows `min(4, floor((MemAvailable - 2 GiB - browsers x 1.2 GiB) / 1.2 GiB / runs))`,
at least 1: 2 GiB for the desktop, 1.2 GiB per worker (the gate's workers measured 0.53 to
0.93 GiB each, a headless Firefox 0.4 GiB), a run that may start a browser counting one.
The gate gives each of its four shards its share (runs 4, browsers 2) and says the choice at
step 4; `scripts/nmas-test` lowers any `-n` (or `auto`) beyond what it allows, saying so on
stderr. A run naming no test file is the full suite: it takes the full-suite lock
(`~/.cache/nmas/full-suite.lock`, the gate holding it for its suite) or refuses, exit 75,
naming the holder. Aimed runs may overlap while the formula allows it.
`nmas-deploy --offline` reports a timeout as TIMED OUT with the running test,
never as a test failure.

`pytest.ini` sets `pythonpath = .`, so both `pytest` and `python -m pytest` work
from the repo root. (Before Phase 0 only the latter did.)

The NetBox step (group A10; the read and import fakes record what they were asked with): every read is of this device and the import is the device's, in its network's repository, as the person; the result carries the import and what was adopted; the step's detail counts what was created and adopted; the adoption record holds each row's device, actor, reason and authority, and with no actor or reason says "Adopt by unknown" and "adopted into management"; NetBox unread before the import, a failed import and an unwritten adoption record each stop at netbox, named or not, with their detail and reason. The profile not sent and the persist step (groups A7a and A8): a profile with nothing to send says why in its row, with and without a reason, applying or not; the save runs as the tool's account (the persist fake records what it was asked with), its answer is in the result and recorded as adopt's for the device, the person and the network; a failed save, named or not, stops with its detail and the whole "do not reload" reason.
